p-list.p-item: Every feature is now free for everyone: cheats, fast-forward up to 6x, unlimited manual save slots, controller button mapping, and advanced core and game settings no longer require Pro.

A new Pro: Pro means unlimited play. Free users can play 10 minutes a day on each platform's free core. Only time spent actually playing counts — not while paused, in a menu or in the background — and it resets at midnight. You'll see how much time is left when a game starts; when it runs out, the game pauses so you can unlock Pro or save and quit.

Each platform has one free core: FCEUmm for NES, Gambatte for Game Boy, PCSX-ReARMed for PlayStation, and the only core on every other platform. The platform's other cores (Nestopia, Mesen, Gearboy, Beetle PSX) require Pro.

Added a welcome offer: for 30 minutes after you first open the Pro page, you can get Lifetime Unlock at a special price, with exactly the same benefits. The page shows a countdown during the offer, and a small countdown badge on the main screens takes you back to the Pro page.

Multi-disc games are now merged on import: discs without an .m3u (cue, chd, iso and more, with names like (Disc 1) and (Disc 2)) become a single game in the Library, with disc switching in the game settings and one memory card shared by all discs.

Arcade BIOS problems show up before a game fails: the launch check reads the BIOS folder directly, so it stays accurate even after files are changed in the Files app, and explains that a broken BIOS blocks every game that uses it. Importing a BIOS that still lacks files now warns you, and importing from the MAME core page recognizes, renames and merges BIOS files just like the Library does, marking incomplete ones — tap to see what's missing.

Sega Mega Drive / Mega-CD games now run on the ClownMDEmu core and Master System / Game Gear games on the Gearsystem core, which also adds SG-1000 support. Both cores are more accurate and support save states, cheats and core options; ClownMDEmu also detects the region from the cartridge, runs .smd files directly and plays Mega-CD games without a BIOS.

Removed the PicoDrive core: its license does not allow use in commercial products, which conflicts with RetroGo's paid features, so it has been replaced by open-source cores whose licenses allow it. 32X and Pico games are no longer supported, and save states made with PicoDrive cannot be loaded by the new cores.
Master System and Game Gear use a new two-button on-screen layout matching the 1 and 2 buttons of the original controllers, and Discover no longer lists platforms that no core can run yet.

Added the MAME arcade core (MAME 0.289), covering Neo Geo, CPS1/CPS2/CPS3, PGM, Cave, NAOMI, Atomiswave and many more arcade boards — most classic arcade games, over 4,000 in all, not counting the different versions of the same game. Arcade games also support local network play, so you can fight in The King of Fighters or team up in Metal Slug on two devices.

Added arcade set management: arcade games are recognized on import and named with their official titles (Chinese titles when the app is in Chinese); BIOS files such as neogeo.zip go straight to the BIOS folder and are merged with any copy already there; before a game starts, missing files are checked and files from its parent set are linked in automatically.

Added the Arcade Library Health report on the MAME core page: see which games are complete and which files are missing, repair one game or all of them, with the original files backed up first. A game's detail page also lets you choose its English or Chinese name for the Library.

Added arcade cheats: import Pugsy's MAME Cheat Collection and most arcade games get cheats — switches, value choices such as weapon or starting stage, and one-tap actions, all with Chinese translations. Until a collection is imported, the cheat page shows a step-by-step guide with screenshots, and you can import the downloaded zip right from the guide without unzipping it.
Added on-screen layouts made for arcade games: six buttons by default, matching arcade fighting games, with a button to switch to a four-button layout during play, plus core options for MAME.
Closing a game is now more thorough and stable, and save-state lists that were sometimes incomplete now show every state.

Added Core Options: tune a core's own settings — aspect ratio, palettes, filters, overclocking, audio processing and more — right from the game settings. Every option is grouped by topic and fully localized, and can be set per core or per game.

Core Options cover all 15 cores and are tailored for RetroGo: options that do not apply on iOS, such as netplay, light guns and mouse input, are left out so they cannot clash with the on-screen turbo buttons, and related options appear or hide based on your current choices — the N64 graphics plugin settings, for example, only show up for the plugin you selected.
Most core options take effect immediately while you play, so you can see the result without leaving the game. The few that need the core to reload are clearly marked as requiring a restart.
The NES cores (FCEUmm, Nestopia and Mesen) can now import a custom palette: choose "Custom", pick a .pal file, and RetroGo places it in that core's BIOS folder for you.
Improved the iPad experience: the tab bar stays at the bottom, matching iPhone, and layout issues when rotating the screen or resizing the window are fixed.
Added the PicoDrive core, bringing support for Sega Mega Drive / Genesis, 32X, Game Gear, Master System, and Mega-CD games.
Expanded the Discover database with Mega Drive titles — browse and look up Mega Drive games right inside the app, with Chinese names that follow the app language.
Added a Mega Drive cheat template database with automatic matching: cheats for supported Mega Drive games can bind to your ROM by CRC32, with no manual setup.

Reworked the save state screen into a sectioned list where you can overwrite an existing save in one tap — not just create new ones — and your save now appears in the list before the screen closes, so you can see it took effect.

Added LAN Multiplayer: host or join a session over the same Wi-Fi network using automatic Bonjour discovery — no setup, no accounts. The room panel shows a live player roster with nicknames, roles, and ping, updated in real time.
Added a Popular Games section to the cheat template catalog, featuring a curated selection of well-known titles per platform for faster access to commonly used cheats.
Added template unbind: manually remove the current system cheat template so the auto-matcher will not re-attach the same template in future sessions.
System cheat templates can now be copied as editable user cheats in one tap — customize any built-in entry without modifying the original template.
The analog stick now features dynamic thumb tracking: the stick base follows your thumb as you drag, and continues responding even when your finger moves outside the original touch zone.
Added Cheats: create custom cheat codes, enable them in game, and browse built-in cheat templates for supported platforms.
Added cheat template search and automatic template matching: RetroGo can use a ROM's CRC32 to look up game metadata and bind a matching cheat template when available.
Cheat templates are now delivered as an optional On-Demand Resource, keeping the base app smaller while allowing the full offline cheat database to be downloaded when needed.
Improved the Discover page by grouping different variants of the same game into one entry, making game browsing cleaner and less repetitive.
Added Chinese game names to the Discover database, so game titles can follow the app language while still preserving authoritative English names where useful.
Improved in-game synchronization with the new GamePauseCoordinator, making menus, sheets, and game resume timing more reliable.
Added a customizable in-game toolbar: rearrange, pin, or hide the top buttons, with the rest tucked into a More menu — set up the in-game bar exactly the way you like it.
Added a landscape lock button to keep the game fixed in landscape while you play.
The entire app now rotates with your device — every screen follows the device orientation, not just the game.
Added Turbo speed levels — Very Slow, Slow, Medium, Fast, Very Fast — configurable per core, and per game.
Added a tap-to-lock Turbo option for the X/Y buttons: a quick tap keeps auto-fire running hands-free, tap again to release — also configurable per core, and per game.
Improved the in-game toolbar icons with subtle shadows so they stay clearly visible even over bright or white game scenes.
Added a Contact Us option in Settings to send feedback by email.
Added in-game disc switching support for multidisc games, including M3U-based game sets.
Added an Acknowledgments page to credit open-source projects, Libretro contributors, and homebrew games used in RetroGo promotional materials.
Introduced a Game Discovery tab powered by On-Demand Resources, letting you browse and look up game information across multiple platforms directly inside the app.
Redesigned the app navigation with a Tab Bar — Library, Discover, and Settings now each live in their own tab for faster access and a cleaner layout.

Overhauled the game library with a fully rearchitected file browser: each page represents a folder in your library, with four view modes — flat icon grid, flat list, grouped by core, grouped by tag, and a tree outline for a full folder hierarchy at a glance.
Added distinctive platform icons for each game system so your library is easier to scan at a glance, along with refined iconography throughout the rest of the app.
Fixed a Turbo button conflict in the custom RetroArch key mapping that prevented acceleration from working correctly in PSP racing games.
Introduced RetroGo Pro to support continued development, with monthly, yearly, and lifetime unlock options.
Added feature access management for Pro-only functionality.
Added per-player external controller mapping with in-app binding configuration.
Added persistent game-level input binding profiles, automatically restored per ROM.
Added configurable core/game options: video driver, audio driver, and mute during fast-forward.
Added overlay touch player assignment and improved virtual/physical input coordination.
Improved stability for Saturn (Yabause) when exiting with connected controllers.
Refactored the runtime architecture by separating RetroArch rendering and game logic, with game logic now running on an independent thread for improved frame stability and responsiveness.
Added fast-forward support with 2x / 3x / 4x / 6x speed levels, reducing repetitive wait time and improving gameplay efficiency.
Integrated signalsmith-stretch for audio smoothing during fast-forward, effectively reducing noise artifacts and improving overall listening quality.
Upgraded configuration to a dual-layer model (core-level + game-level): set defaults per core and override them per game for finer-grained personalization.
Added a new SpriteKit-based Overlay buttons system to improve the in-game control and interaction experience.
Added smart multi-file ROM import detection for both file import and folder import workflows.
The importer can now automatically recognize grouped game files such as cue, m3u, gdi, mds, and ccd, detect missing referenced files, and handle grouped imports more reliably.
Enhanced data security by migrating core files (Roms, Save States, Databases, etc.) to a secure system directory, preventing accidental deletion and ensuring a more stable app experience.
RetroGo was officially released on the App Store.
